title: CFD Credibility for Hinge Washout in a Bileaflet Mechanical Valve: Three Models, Two Mechanisms, and Risk-Informed Scoring Under ASME V&V 40
device: Adult-size bileaflet mechanical heart valve (aortic position), hinge-region washout

models.name: Model A: FSI-informed LES
models.what_it_computes: Transient large-eddy simulation of pulsatile flow with prescribed leaflet kinematics; outputs include hinge-region velocity fields, instantaneous shear rate, Lagrangian particle residence time, and washout time constants.

models.name: Model B: Steady RANS with Porous-Hinge Surrogates
models.what_it_computes: Time-averaged Reynolds-averaged Navier–Stokes with porous-joint representations for sub-gap leakage; outputs include mean hinge through-flow, scalar washout index, and near-wall shear proxies.

models.name: Model C: Lattice–Boltzmann Microscale Hinge CFD
models.what_it_computes: Voxel-resolved hinge recess simulation from micro-CT geometry; computes full Lagrangian residence-time distributions, escape probabilities, and shear exposure metrics during systolic/diastolic phases.

mechanisms.name: Mechanism 1: Diastolic leakage-driven washout
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Reverse-pressure leakage jets during valve closure are a primary driver of contaminant and platelet clearance from hinge recesses when bulk forward flow is absent.

mechanisms.name: Mechanism 2: Systolic vortex-pumping washout
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Forward-flow shear layers and hinge-adjacent vortices entrain hinge fluid and promote exchange with the main stream, affecting residence time during peak ejection.

deviation.detail: All credibility factors are scored on a 0–7 integer scale per model–mechanism pair, where 0 indicates no supporting evidence and 7 indicates comprehensive evidence.

sections: Context of Use (ASME V&V 40): CFD predictions of hinge washout will be used to demonstrate equivalence of a modified hinge geometry to a reference design under aortic pulsatile conditions, to support reduced benchtop dye-visualization testing for the modification; predictions are limited to in-vitro ranges consistent with ISO 5840 test loops

Model Risk Analysis (ASME V&V 40): Model influence = High (CFD is the primary evidence for hinge washout equivalence); Decision consequence = Medium (impacts scope of benchtop testing but does not directly guide clinical use); Overall model risk = High with rationale
Computational Models: A (FSI-informed LES), B (Steady RANS with porous-hinge surrogates), C (Lattice–Boltzmann microscale CFD)
